summary_paragraph: The patient was admitted with fevers, vomiting, and malaise after cutting her toe at a new gym. She was found to have E. coli bacteremia likely originating from a urinary tract infection, despite lacking typical urinary symptoms. She was started on broad-spectrum antibiotics and later transitioned to ceftriaxone after cultures confirmed pan-sensitive E. coli. She developed antibiotic-associated diarrhea, which improved with loperamide; C. difficile was ruled out. A right upper lobe lung opacity was noted on imaging, but it resolved without specific treatment and fungal studies were negative. Her transplant kidney function initially declined but normalized with hydration and antibiotics. A PICC line was placed for outpatient IV antibiotic therapy. She was discharged to a rehab facility on IV ceftriaxone, oral vancomycin, and loperamide, with follow-up planned in infectious disease and nephrology clinics.
problems: Septicemia due to escherichia coli [E. coli]
